From e3668b371329ea036ff022ce8ecc82f8befcf003 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sergey Senozhatsky <senozhatsky@chromium.org>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 16:42:44 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] zram: do not forget to endio for partial discard requests

As reported by Qu Wenruo and Avinesh Kumar, the following

 getconf PAGESIZE
 65536
 blkdiscard -p 4k /dev/zram0

takes literally forever to complete.  zram doesn't support partial
discards and just returns immediately w/o doing any discard work in such
cases.  The problem is that we forget to endio on our way out, so
blkdiscard sleeps forever in submit_bio_wait().  Fix this by jumping to
end_bio label, which does bio_endio().

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/20260331074255.777019-1-senozhatsky@chromium.org
Fixes: 0120dd6e4e20 ("zram: make zram_bio_discard more self-contained")
Signed-off-by: Sergey Senozhatsky <senozhatsky@chromium.org>
Reported-by: Qu Wenruo <wqu@suse.com>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-block/92361cd3-fb8b-482e-bc89-15ff1acb9a59@suse.com
Tested-by: Qu Wenruo <wqu@suse.com>
Reported-by: Avinesh Kumar <avinesh.kumar@suse.com>
Closes: https://bugzilla.suse.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1256530
Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Cc: Brian Geffon <bgeffon@google.com>
Cc: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
Cc: Minchan Kim <minchan@kernel.org>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/block/zram/zram_drv.c b/drivers/block/zram/zram_drv.c
index c2afd1c34f4a..43b68fdd95d6 100644
--- a/drivers/block/zram/zram_drv.c
+++ b/drivers/block/zram/zram_drv.c
@@ -2678,7 +2678,7 @@ static void zram_bio_discard(struct zram *zram, struct bio *bio)
 	 */
 	if (offset) {
 		if (n <= (PAGE_SIZE - offset))
-			return;
+			goto end_bio;
 
 		n -= (PAGE_SIZE - offset);
 		index++;
@@ -2693,6 +2693,7 @@ static void zram_bio_discard(struct zram *zram, struct bio *bio)
 		n -= PAGE_SIZE;
 	}
 
+end_bio:
 	bio_endio(bio);
 }
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File modified: `drivers/block/zram/zram_drv.c`

**Modification in function `zram_bio_discard`:**

- **Early exit bug fix:** When a partial discard request (with a non-zero offset that doesn't cover a full page) is detected, the original code used a `return` statement, which caused the function to exit without calling `bio_endio()`. This led to the caller (e.g., `blkdiscard`) waiting indefinitely.

- **Change:** Replaced the `return` with a `goto end_bio`. This transfers control to the newly added label `end_bio`, which ensures `bio_endio(bio)` is always executed.

- **New label:** Added the label `end_bio` after the loop that performs the actual discard. The original `bio_endio(bio)` that existed after the loop is now referenced by this label, making it reachable from both the normal discard completion path and the partial discard early exit path.

### Relationships between modifications

- Both changes are part of a single logical fix: ensuring that every path through `zram_bio_discard` calls `bio_endio(bio)` before returning.
- The addition of the `end_bio` label is necessary to create a common endpoint that the partial discard case can jump to, while also preserving the existing normal discard behavior.
- The fix directly addresses the bug described in the commit: partial discard requests were never completed, causing infinite blocking. The modifications guarantee that the bio is always ended, regardless of whether the discard is supported or not.

Here is the commit message:
zram: do not forget to endio for partial discard requests

As reported by Qu Wenruo and Avinesh Kumar, the following

 getconf PAGESIZE
 65536
 blkdiscard -p 4k /dev/zram0

takes literally forever to complete.  zram doesn't support partial
discards and just returns immediately w/o doing any discard work in such
cases.  The problem is that we forget to endio on our way out, so
blkdiscard sleeps forever in submit_bio_wait().  Fix this by jumping to
end_bio label, which does bio_endio().

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/20260331074255.777019-1-senozhatsky@chromium.org
Fixes: 0120dd6e4e20 ("zram: make zram_bio_discard more self-contained")
Signed-off-by: Sergey Senozhatsky <senozhatsky@chromium.org>
Reported-by: Qu Wenruo <wqu@suse.com>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-block/92361cd3-fb8b-482e-bc89-15ff1acb9a59@suse.com
Tested-by: Qu Wenruo <wqu@suse.com>
Reported-by: Avinesh Kumar <avinesh.kumar@suse.com>
Closes: https://bugzilla.suse.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1256530
Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Cc: Brian Geffon <bgeffon@google.com>
Cc: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
Cc: Minchan Kim <minchan@kernel.org>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
In `zram_bio_discard`, when a partial discard request is detected (non-zero offset with insufficient bytes to fill a page), the function returns immediately without calling `bio_endio`, leaving the bio unfinished and causing `submit_bio_wait` to wait forever.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void zram_bio_discard(struct zram *zram, struct bio *bio)
 {
 	size_t n = bio->bi_iter.bi_size;
 	u32 index = bio->bi_iter.bi_sector >> SECTORS_PER_PAGE_SHIFT;
 	u32 offset = (bio->bi_iter.bi_sector & (SECTORS_PER_PAGE - 1)) <<
 			SECTOR_SHIFT;
 
 	/*
 	 * zram manages data in physical block size units. Because logical block
 	 * size isn't identical with physical block size on some arch, we
 	 * could get a discard request pointing to a specific offset within a
 	 * certain physical block.  Although we can handle this request by
 	 * reading that physiclal block and decompressing and partially zeroing
 	 * and re-compressing and then re-storing it, this isn't reasonable
 	 * because our intent with a discard request is to save memory.  So
 	 * skipping this logical block is appropriate here.
 	 */
 	if (offset) {
 		if (n <= (PAGE_SIZE - offset))
-			return;
+			goto end_bio;
 
 		n -= (PAGE_SIZE - offset);
 		index++;
 	}
 
 	while (n >= PAGE_SIZE) {
 		slot_lock(zram, index);
 		slot_free(zram, index);
 		slot_unlock(zram, index);
 		atomic64_inc(&zram->stats.notify_free);
 		index++;
 		n -= PAGE_SIZE;
 	}
 
+end_bio:
 	bio_endio(bio);
 }
